Docs/Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting

Diagnose installation, artifact access, rendering and protocol mismatches before spending time on a training run.

Check the checkout and dependencies first

Run commands from the public repository root in the intended Python environment. Import tasks before creating a Gym environment and use the current <Task>-<Hand>-v1 ID. The installation guide pins Gymnasium 0.29.1 and LeRobot 0.4.0; newer dependency resolution is not automatically equivalent.

The functional tests need no downloaded demonstrations or checkpoints. They check task tables, contracts and baseline interfaces, not policy success. Keep their output and source revision when reporting a regression.

python -m pip show torch mani_skill gymnasium lerobot
python -m pytest tests -q

Dataset access or missing meshes

SymptomWhat to check
Hub download returns 401/403Request access to the gated dataset repository ↗ and run hf auth login in the environment performing the download. Never paste your token into a bug report.
Missing task-object meshDownload assets/** with --local-dir tasks; files should be under tasks/assets/task_object_meshes/, not an extra nested assets directory.
Checkpoint not foundUse the exact published method directory. ACT/DP use current task IDs; π0.5 packages may keep their trained legacy directory names while evaluation takes the current ID.
GR00T backbone access failsAccept the gated backbone terms or use the documented local backbone path. GR00T has its own runtime and model-access requirements.

GPU, Vulkan and camera failures

CPU physics does not eliminate the GPU/Vulkan requirement for rendering. Confirm the NVIDIA driver and a PyTorch wheel supporting your GPU. RTX 50-series hardware needs the compatible CUDA build described in Installation. A blank viewport should be fixed before interpreting any policy score.

Tasks whose recordings change render-body visibility need the CPU path for pixel-demo rendering; the training guide names the known example. Reduce render batch size or continue with the renderer's supported chunking options rather than changing the camera preset to make a failing run fit. pixel-rendering guide ↗ documents these restrictions.

Fingerprint drift and weak checkpoint results

fingerprint DRIFT means the recording and task build are not admitted as compatible. The validators resolve the measured record-neutral lineages in tasks/config/fingerprint_lineage.py ↗; other changed task behavior remains incompatible. An !! INCOMPLETE worker result is not a release-success rate.

If a checkpoint loads but performs poorly, verify the camera preset, image size, ordered state channels, horizon, seed list and action processing before changing the policy. DP execution chunk size and GR00T instruction sampling materially affect the protocol. See Evaluation for method-specific settings and distinctions between paper and released checkpoints.

Prepare a minimal, public-safe report

Include the exact command with secrets removed, source commit, current environment ID, dependency versions, relevant traceback and the smallest reproducible case. Do not upload access tokens, private filesystem paths or complete gated artifacts.

Open an issue in the official code repository ↗. For result reproducibility, include the experiment record and distinguish a functional smoke test from a full evaluation.
